hero: Wisconsin cross-country ski conditions built around Birkie country, Northwoods snow, state-park grooming and the short snow windows that matter farther south.
sourceStory: Wisconsin is unusually well suited to a decision board because Travel Wisconsin already publishes volunteer-reported cross-country conditions while Wisconsin DNR properties maintain their own winter trail rules and status. This tool keeps those reports separate from the modeled snow and surface engine.

regions.name: Northwest / Birkie Country
regions.blurb: Hayward, Cable, Bayfield and the Lake Superior snowbelt: Wisconsin's deepest Nordic culture and one of its most reliable natural-snow zones.

regions.name: Northwoods
regions.blurb: Minocqua, Manitowish Waters, Mercer and Three Lakes, where cold retention and lake-effect patterns often preserve skiing when central Wisconsin thaws.

regions.name: Northeast / Door County
regions.blurb: Door County, Green Bay and the northeast forests: classic and skate systems influenced by Lake Michigan and Green Bay.

regions.name: Central Wisconsin
regions.blurb: Wausau, Iola, Clark County and Chippewa-area systems with strong club grooming and variable storm tracks.

regions.name: Madison / Southwest
regions.blurb: Blue Mound and southwest Wisconsin: terrain-rich skiing where freeze-thaw timing often matters as much as total snow.

regions.name: Southeast / Kettle Moraine
regions.blurb: Lapham Peak and Kettle Moraine: Wisconsin's most important marginal-snow decision zone, including lighted and snowmaking-supported options.

faqs.q: How are Wisconsin XC conditions different from the model?
faqs.a: The snow and surface engine is modeled. Travel Wisconsin, Wisconsin DNR and trail operators remain the source of truth for grooming, closures and actual trail condition.

faqs.q: Which Wisconsin trails are most resilient in poor natural snow?
faqs.a: Snowmaking-supported systems such as Lapham Peak and Mt. Telemark can behave very differently from nearby natural-snow trails, so the board flags snowmaking separately rather than treating modeled depth as the whole story.

faqs.q: Do Wisconsin skiers need a trail pass?
faqs.a: Pass rules vary by property. Wisconsin state properties may require a state trail pass for adult skiers, while club, county and private systems can use their own pass or donation rules. Each trail page points to the operator source.

trails.name: American Birkebeiner Trail System
trails.description: A 100+ km Nordic system linking Cable and Hayward, with dedicated classic and skate terrain and snowmaking loops at Mt. Telemark Village.

trails.name: Mt. Ashwabay Nordic Trails
trails.description: Roughly 40 km of regularly groomed classic and skate trail near Lake Superior, with volunteer grooming and strong snowbelt exposure.

trails.name: Brule River State Forest
trails.description: State-forest Nordic skiing in far northwest Wisconsin, where Lake Superior snow and cold can preserve natural coverage.

trails.name: Copper Falls State Park
trails.description: A rugged northern state-park system groomed for classic and skate when snow allows, with colder terrain east of Ashland.

trails.name: Minocqua Winter Park
trails.description: A large destination Nordic network south of Minocqua with classic, skate, rentals and a chalet in the heart of the Northwoods.

trails.name: WinMan Trails
trails.description: A multi-use Northwoods trail system with winter grooming for classic and skate skiing near Manitowish Waters.

trails.name: MECCA Trails
trails.description: Volunteer-supported Mercer-area skiing with classic and skate terrain and direct seasonal condition reporting.

trails.name: Three Eagle Trail
trails.description: A Northwoods rail-trail corridor between Three Lakes and Eagle River with groomed winter skiing when conditions permit.

trails.name: Peninsula State Park
trails.description: Door County classic skiing through forest and bluff terrain, with Lake Michigan moderation making timing and snow retention important.

trails.name: Ariens Nordic Center
trails.description: A purpose-built Nordic venue near Brillion with classic and skate grooming and machine-made snow capability.

trails.name: Nine Mile Recreation Area
trails.description: A major Wausau-area county Nordic network known for classic and skate grooming and varied terrain.

trails.name: Iola Winter Sports Club
trails.description: More than 20 km of club-groomed classic and skate trails with rentals, ski jumping and direct club condition reporting.

trails.name: Levis / Trow Mound
trails.description: Clark County forest skiing with classic and skate grooming across rolling central-Wisconsin terrain.

trails.name: Lake Wissota State Park
trails.description: State-park skiing near Chippewa Falls with classic and skate grooming when the natural-snow base is adequate.

trails.name: Blue Mound State Park
trails.description: High-relief southwest Wisconsin skiing where elevation can help preserve snow but thaw timing remains critical.

trails.name: Lapham Peak
trails.description: A key southeast Wisconsin Nordic system with classic and skate grooming, lighted night skiing and a snowmaking-supported loop.

trails.name: Kettle Moraine Southern Unit - McMiller
trails.description: Classic and skate terrain in the Southern Kettle Moraine, where southern-Wisconsin snow windows can be short and freeze-thaw timing matters.

trails.name: Kettle Moraine Northern Unit
trails.description: A broad east-central Wisconsin forest network with both groomed and ungroomed Nordic mileage across glacial terrain.
